tone.notes: Curious and clear; one true story with a concrete point ('your map would drift more than ten kilometres a day'); the kicker ties back to the hook. No hype words.

visuals.notes: A new picture per sentence; satellite/phone/clock props make each step concrete; title on one line; captions clear of faces; Ori visible on dark skies thanks to the pale outline.

character.notes: Ori on-model (bubble helmet, bun, navy tunic) in every scene; mouth follows the voice.

learnings: The 'point' beat works best as a consequence for the viewer ('your map would drift…'), not as 'this changed science'.
On night/space scenes, put numbers on a sign — hand-lettered text is low-contrast on dark skies.
Very short sentences (e.g. 'That sounds like nothing.') get a scene for under a second; merge them into the next sentence's scene.
